findings.title: Partial multi-segment packet published/consumed but not counted as sent
findings.explanation: Ring space is only checked one segment at a time. If the inner loop exits via goto end_of_tx after some segments of a packet were copied (ring full, zero-length desc, NULL remap), txq->last_used, sw_ring and tx_used are already updated for those segments. nb_tx is not incremented and nb_tx_free is not decremented. When nb_tx>0, used_cnt is published including the trailing segments, which have no NTB_FLAG_EOP, so the peer merges a truncated packet with the next one. The caller thinks the packet was not sent and may free or resend it, but sw_ring still references its segments, so ntb_enqueue_cleanup later frees them again (double free or use-after-free). nb_tx_free also drifts above the real free count. When nb_tx==0, last_used still moves forward but nothing is published, so local and peer ring state go out of sync permanently.
findings.suggestion: Before touching any state, check that the whole packet fits: the free descriptors between last_used and avail_cnt must be >= nb_segs, otherwise break. If a per-segment error happens mid-packet, roll txq->last_used and nb_mbufs back to their values at the start of the packet, clear the sw_ring entries for that packet, and then exit.

findings.title: Descriptor count used as packet limit; reads past used_cnt for multi-seg
findings.explanation: used_nb counts used descriptors, but count limits the outer loop, which counts packets. The inner while loop can use several descriptors per packet and never checks rxq->last_used against used_cnt. With multi-segment packets (for example used_nb=4 made of two 2-segment packets), the loop keeps going after all published descriptors are used. It reads used-ring entries the peer has not written yet, hands the stale mbufs in sw_ring to the caller, and posts replacement descriptors for slots the peer still owns. RX_MISS stats are inflated as well.
findings.suggestion: Track the remaining descriptors: stop the outer loop when rxq->last_used reaches used_cnt, and in the inner loop make sure a full packet up to EOP is available before consuming it.

findings.title: Mbuf alloc failure drops packet and desynchronizes rx ring
findings.explanation: buffers[nb_rx] is set and rxq->last_used is advanced before the replacement mbuf is allocated. If the allocation fails, goto end_of_rx skips nb_rx++, so the packet (and any segments already chained) is not reported. That mbuf leaks once its sw_ring slot is overwritten, and last_avail is now permanently one slot closer to last_used. If nb_rx==0 and earlier segments of this packet were refilled, sw_ring and last_avail were advanced but their rx_desc entries are never written to the peer. The next publish sets avail_cnt beyond them, so the peer sees descriptors still holding addresses of mbufs already handed to the application and DMAs into memory the application owns.
findings.suggestion: Allocate the replacement mbuf before consuming the used entry, or roll back the partial packet on failure (restore last_used and last_avail to their values at packet start and unlink the chain). Always write any prepared rx_desc entries before updating avail_cnt.

findings.title: Mbuf alloc failure loses in-progress packet and corrupts ring state
findings.explanation: buffers[nb_rx] is set and rxq->last_used is advanced before the replacement mbuf is allocated. On allocation failure, goto end_of_rx skips nb_rx++, so the packet (and any segments already chained) is never reported to the caller and leaks. The consumed slot is never refilled, and last_used has moved past it. If nb_rx==0, the rx_desc entries already prepared for earlier segments are thrown away even though sw_ring and last_avail were updated, so the avail ring is left out of sync.
findings.suggestion: Allocate the replacement mbuf before consuming the used entry. On failure, stop without advancing last_used or last_avail and leave the descriptor posted.

findings.title: used_cnt published before write barrier
findings.explanation: The payload copies and used-ring entries go to the peer BAR (often write-combining). *txq->used_cnt is updated before rte_wmb(), so those stores can become visible to the peer after the counter. The peer can then read stale len/flags or incomplete payload. ntb_queue_init puts the barrier before the counter store, which is the correct order.
findings.suggestion: Call rte_wmb() after the rte_memcpy calls and before '*txq->used_cnt = txq->last_used;'.

findings.title: avail_cnt published before write barrier
findings.explanation: New rx descriptors are written to the peer-visible ring through the BAR mapping, and avail_cnt is updated before rte_wmb(). The peer can see the new avail_cnt before the descriptor addr/len stores land. It then reads stale descriptors and writes payload into a buffer that has already been handed to the application.
findings.suggestion: Call rte_wmb() after the rx_desc_ring rte_memcpy calls and before '*rxq->avail_cnt = rxq->last_avail;'.

findings.title: Off-by-one in range check accepts the address one past the MW end
findings.explanation: The upper bound uses <=, so the address peer_mw_base[i] + mw_size[i] counts as inside window i. That address is one byte past the window. It gets mapped to base + mw_size, which is outside the mapped BAR, and any access through it goes out of bounds. This confirms prior finding 2d4aec34533b, but the comparison is on line 175, not line 174.
findings.suggestion: Use a strict upper bound: `addr < hw->peer_mw_base[i] + hw->mw_size[i]`.

findings.title: Off-by-one in range check allows address one past MW end
findings.explanation: The upper bound uses <=, so an address equal to base+size (one past the window) is treated as inside and maps beyond the BAR.

refuted.title: Truncation mutates caller mbuf data_len without fixing pkt_len
refuted.explanation: When the payload is larger than the remote buffer, txm->data_len is shortened in place but pkt_len is not updated. The caller's mbuf is left with inconsistent lengths, and the data is silently truncated while the packet is still counted as sent.
refuted.suggestion: Use a local copy length instead of writing to txm->data_len, or treat the oversize case as an error.
